claims.text: The target material is a Ta-based refractory high-entropy alloy in a disordered liquid state near its melting point.
Standard ab initio thermodynamic integration is prohibitively expensive because extensive liquid-phase-space sampling is needed to converge free-energy differences.
Standard EAM potentials fail to capture complex liquid structure and chemical SRO, causing inaccurate free-energy predictions.
Moment Tensor Potentials have been used successfully to represent SRO-containing solid MoNbTaW and simulate its dislocation behavior.
Deep Potential models have shown success in capturing SRO in solid refractory BCC systems.
Chemical SRO and ordered clusters can measurably alter properties of solid refractory high-entropy alloys.
Liquid-state chemical SRO and local clusters are critical to obtaining accurate free energies in multicomponent refractory alloys.
An MTP or DP trained on liquid AIMD configurations can model the local energy fluctuations associated with liquid SRO.
The proposed potential should be trained on high-temperature liquid configurations of representative refractory systems such as MoNbTaW or WTaMoNbV.
The cited WTaMoNbV evidence provides a context for obtaining liquid training configurations.
A perturbative or alchemical free-energy scheme can replace direct ab initio integration over the full phase space by sampling a reduced configuration set.
Machine-learning potentials are orders of magnitude faster than AIMD and therefore permit enough liquid sampling to converge the free energy.
Solid-state evidence shows that SRO in MoNbTaW affects screw-dislocation mobility and strengthening.
The proposed calculations should operate from 2000 K to 3000 K at 1 atm, with nanosecond sampling sufficient to equilibrate liquid SRO.
The perturbation scheme will predict free energy of mixing and melting temperature within 5% of ab initio TI or experimental trends.
The proposed method will reduce computational cost by more than 90%, changing simulation time from weeks to days.
The method will correctly predict liquid SRO and thereby improve phase-stability predictions in Ta-based RHEAs.
Transfer may fail for compositions outside the training domain, for rare liquid configurations, for extreme segregation, or for electronic effects absent from the training data.
Comparison against limited ab initio TI and AIMD liquid structure factors can distinguish a genuine speedup from an artifact caused by inadequate liquid training coverage.
